papers.title: Small sums of roots of unity: polylogarithmic exceptional sets and conditional separation
papers.abstract: We prove a polylogarithmic exceptional-set estimate for symmetric five-term sums of roots of unity of arbitrary order. More precisely, at most $O((\log(2N))^{11})$ points of the $N$-grid satisfy $|1+2\cos(2\pi x)+2\cos(2\pi y)|<\exp(-C(\log(2N))^{13})$. This implies the corresponding bound for small conjugates at the reduced conductor: outside polylogarithmically many real embeddings, every such sum is at least quasipolynomially large. The proof is unconditional and combines a polynomial-vector-field multiplicity estimate, arithmetic jet determinants, analytic propagation, and interpolation determinants for nearby grid points. As a companion result, assuming a uniform number-field $abc$ conjecture, we prove that every sum of a fixed number of distinct prime-order roots of unity has modulus at least $\exp(-\varepsilon p)$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large primes $p$, uniformly in the exponents. That proof uses simultaneous compression of the exponents, discriminant estimates, and cyclic resultants.

papers.title: Post-quantum commutative group actions from oriented superspecial abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We study the cryptographic use of Shimura class group actions on superspecial principally polarized abelian varieties equipped with a CM orientation, within the context of post-quantum cryptography. Besides giving an accessible introduction to the topic, illustrated with many examples, we provide tools for representing CM orientations through higher-dimensional isogenies and for computing the Shimura class group action in the restricted effective group action model. Here, key auxiliary results are a version of Kani's lemma "with CM" and a trick that often allows to halve the ambient dimension. We also give a method for finding superspecial principally polarized abelian surfaces that are oriented by a given CM order, which is extracted from an algebraic framework for studying CM orientations using the Ibukiyama-Katsura-Oort correspondence. We also analyze obstructions to transitivity of the Shimura class group action, related to the characteristic-zero notion of CM type.

papers.title: Rational analytic prismatization
papers.abstract: We develop a general theory of analytic prismatization with $\mathbb{Q}_p$-coefficients in rigid analytic geometry over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We prove an equivalence of perfect complexes on the perfect analytic prismatization modulo Frobenius with perfect complexes on the relative Fargues--Fontaine curve for any smooth partially proper rigid analytic variety. In particular, we explain how this equivalence conceptualizes the decompletion techniques by passing to locally analytic vectors which appear in (geometric) Sen theory

papers.title: The stacky approach to de Rham-Witt cohomology
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. Ekedahl proved an equivalence of triangulated categories between bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring and complexes of $F$-gauges. We give a geometric proof, independent of his proof, that the de Rham-Witt realization is a symmetric monoidal equivalence of stable $\infty$-categories between perfect $F$-gauges and bounded coherent complexes over the Raynaud ring with Ekedahl's completed star product, as expected by Illusie. The geometry comes from topological restriction homology: $\mathrm{TR}^r(k;\mathbf Z_p)^{hS^1}$ is an iterated fibre product of copies of $\mathrm{TC}^-(k;\mathbf Z_p)$, and taking even stacks before and after the fibre product gives the genuine and the naive $r$-Nygaard stacks. Pushforward from the genuine to the naive $r$-Nygaard stack realizes Andriopoulos' $r$-Nygaard filtrations, which interpolate between the Nygaard filtration at $r=1$ and the Hodge-Witt filtration at $r=\infty$. On the genuine $r$-Nygaard stack, which is a chain of Nygaard charts, restriction and Frobenius come from the inclusions of sub-chains, Verschiebung from duality, and the differential as a Bockstein operator, and the relations of the star product become projection formulas. As applications, we deduce Ekedahl's K\"unneth formula and Poincar\'e duality for de Rham-Witt cohomology from their counterparts for $F$-gauge cohomology, and show that the special-value formulas of Illusie and of Mondal over finite fields are equivalent.

papers.title: Upper Bounds on the de Bruijn-Newman constant for Dirichlet $L$-functions with primitive real-valued characters
papers.abstract: Let $\chi_m$ be a primitive real-valued Dirichlet character of conductor $m\ge3$, let $L(s)=L(s,\chi_m)$ be the associated Dirichlet $L$-function, and let $\xi_L(s)$ denote its completed form. For each $t \in \mathbb R,$ we define the entire function \[ H^L_t(z) := \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} e^{tu^2}\, \Phi_L(u)\, e^{izu}\, du, \] where $\Phi_L$ is the superexponentially decaying density \[ \Phi_L(u) := \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \xi_L\!\left(\frac{1+is}{2}\right) e^{-isu}\, ds. \] The family $\{H_t^L\}_{t \in \mathbb R}$ describes the heat-flow evolution of $\xi_L$ and solves a backward heat equation. By the work of Newman, there exists a finite constant $\Lambda_L$, called the generalized de Bruijn--Newman constant, such that all the zeros of $H_t^L$ are real if and only if $t \ge \Lambda_L$. The Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH) for $L$ is equivalent to the assertion that $\Lambda_L \le 0$. Dobner established the matching lower bound $\Lambda_L \ge 0$, while de Bruijn proved the upper bound $\Lambda_L \le \tfrac12$. We prove the unconditional uniform bound $\Lambda_L\le953/3200=0.2978125$ for every primitive real-valued character of conductor $3\le m\le400$, together with stronger individual bounds. The proof extends the effective approximation of Polymath to Dirichlet $L$-functions, retaining the conductor dependence in the error estimates. We combine these estimates with Platt's numerical verification of GRH by Platt and rigorous interval computations. We also give conditional bounds under explicit global initial zero-strip hypotheses, including $|\operatorname{Im}z|\le3/4$ for the zeros of $H_0^L$.

papers.title: The Projective Reed-Muller Code from Quartic Curves in the Projective Plane
papers.abstract: We study the Hamming weight enumerator of the projective Reed-Muller code $\mathcal C_{2,4}$ over $\mathbf F_q$, with $\operatorname{char}(\mathbf F_q)>3$. We determine the geometrically reducible and singular contributions by combining incidence counts with counts of plane linear series on a fixed normalization. The line and conic configurations and the genus zero cases give explicit polynomials. The line-cubic and genus one cases give formulas involving class numbers. The genus two contribution is a finite sum over hyperelliptic models, using their point counts over $\mathbf F_q$ and $\mathbf F_{q^2}$ and their rational Weierstrass points. The remaining smooth contribution is the weighted point count distribution of nonhyperelliptic genus three curves.

papers.title: Unconditional Subexponential Arithmetic Circuits\ for Positive Factorial Multiples
papers.abstract: Let $\tau(n)$ be the least number of binary additions, subtractions and multiplications required to construct $n$ from $1$ and $2$, with reuse of intermediate values. We show that, for every sufficiently large integer $k$, some positive integer $m$ satisfies \[ \tau(mk!)\leq \exp\!\left(O\!\left((\log k)^{2/3}(\log\log k)^{1/3}\right)\right). \] The proof combines unconditional results of Lenstra, Pila and Pomerance on smooth numbers in short intervals and on orders of genus-two Jacobians with a five-parameter family carrying a rational divisor class of infinite order. We encode rational divisor arithmetic, including the tests determining its branches, by a nonzero division-free integer circuit. A common finite sampling space yields circuits whose outputs collectively contain every prime at most $k$, and repeated squaring supplies the required factorial valuations. The circuit bound includes the cost of constructing all integer parameters. This work was carried out with assistance from the UniMath model, developed by UniDT (Shanghai) Co., Ltd., and GPT-6.1 Sol.

papers.title: Bowen--Franks groups and minus class groups of imaginary abelian fields
papers.abstract: $\mathrm{Lei}$, $\mathrm{M\ddot{u}ller}$, and $\mathrm{Valli\grave{e}res}$ constructed a directed graph for which the torsion part of the corresponding Bowen--Franks group is related to the minus part of the class group of a cyclotomic number field with prime conductor. We extend this result to a general imaginary abelian field.

papers.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
papers.abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.

papers.title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
papers.abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

papers.title: Simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets
papers.abstract: Visibility from the origin in integer lattices is a well-studied problem. More recently, the corresponding question for cut-and-project sets has attracted attention. We consider simultaneous visibility, which asks what points in a set are visible from every point of another set. This question was studied for the integer lattice by Rearick and Rumsey, among others. In this work, we investigate simultaneous visibility in cut-and-project sets associated with real quadratic fields satisfying the Hammarhjelm condition. Under suitable geometric conditions on the finite set, we prove that the density of the simultaneously visible points exists and derive an explicit formula for it. We also examine simultaneous visibility in more general cut-and-project sets under a condition on the associated lattice.

papers.title: Simultaneous popular differences for polynomial and linear progressions in finite fields
papers.abstract: We study simultaneous popular differences for polynomial progressions and linear progressions over finite fields $\mathbb F_p$. For certain families of polynomial progressions of algebraic complexity $1$, such as $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^3, x+2y^3)$, we prove the existence of $y \neq 0$ which is popular simultaneously for both progressions. This extends previous results by Conlon, Dong and Hong who considered complexity $0$ progressions. On the other hand, we construct counterexamples showing that simultaneous popular differences are not guaranteed to exist for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y^2, x+2y^2)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x, x+y, x+3y)$, or for $(x, x+y, x+2y)$ and $(x,x+y,x+2y,x+3y)$, answering questions posed by Conlon, Dong and Hong.

papers.title: A Joint Local Limit Theorem for Prime Divisor Counting Functions
papers.abstract: We establish a uniform two-dimensional local limit theorem for the joint distribution of $\Omega(n)$ and $\Omega(n+1)$. More precisely, along a set of scales of logarithmic density one, the normalized joint counts are uniformly approximated by the density of two independent Gaussian random variables, each with mean and variance $\log\log x$, up to a power-saving error. The proof builds upon a recent circle-method framework of Tao and Ter\"av\"ainen. Our results equally hold for the additive function $\omega$. Additionally, we explore applications of our local limit theorem in the setting of uniquely ergodic systems.

papers.title: An alternating Mizuno formula, modified gamma functions, and double sine special values
papers.abstract: For $n\ge1$ and $\operatorname{Re}(x_j)>0$, we prove an alternating analogue of Mizuno's product formula: \begin{equation*} \prod\nolimits_{m=0}^{\infty} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{n}(m+x_j)\right)^{(-1)^m} = \frac{(\sqrt{\pi/2})^n} {\prod_{j=1}^{n}\widetilde{\Gamma}(x_j)}, \end{equation*} where $\widetilde{\Gamma}$ is the modified gamma function associated with the alternating Hurwitz zeta function. The polynomial factors are regularized using factorwise logarithms, and the formula establishes compatibility between this regularization and polynomial factorization. Applications include Gaussian and cyclotomic (Kurokawa--Wakayama type) evaluations; the single-factor case recovers the alternating Lerch formula, and a normalized ratio yields Wallis' product. A second group of results concerns an alternating double sine-type function. At nonexceptional positive periods, its positive-integer special values admit finite tangent-product representations. These products define locally meromorphic continuations $F_m$ in the period parameter. For $m\ge2$ and nonzero algebraic parameters, the continued values belong to $\mathbb P^1(\overline{\mathbb Q})$ at rational parameters and are finite, nonzero, and transcendental at nonrational parameters. We determine their orders at rational parameters and distinguish parameter continuation from fixed-period specialization at exceptional parameters. Additional results include Barnes factorizations of multiple alternating gamma functions, a Glaisher--Kinkelin special value, finite-product Stirling-type asymptotics, a symmetric two-parameter form of the known odd-integer multiplication formula, and an odd-scaling distribution relation for the alternating double sine-type function.

papers.title: Transcendence of dendric beta-expansions with pure discrete spectrum
papers.abstract: We prove the transcendence of numbers that have $\beta$-expansions (in algebraic bases $\beta$) belonging to dendric shifts with pure discrete spectrum, under combinatorial conditions on their directive sequences of substitutions. This includes Arnoux-Rauzy sequences on arbitrary alphabets and Cassaigne-Selmer sequences. The proof uses Rauzy fractals and the subspace theorem.

papers.title: Galois Groups of Shifted Exponential Polynomials
papers.abstract: For a fixed integer $a>0$, consider the shifted truncations \[ F_{n,a}(x)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}\frac{x^j}{(a+j)!} \] and their monic integral normalizations $P_{n,a}(x)=(n+a)!F_{n,a}(x)$. In this paper, we prove that, for every fixed integer $a>0$, the set of $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible has natural density one. We also prove that $G_{n,a}:=\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})$ is primitive for all sufficiently large $n$ for which $F_{n,a}$ is irreducible, and that it contains $A_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. Finally, we prove that, for any fixed integer $a>0$, the discriminant of $F_{n,a}$ is a nonsquare for a density-one set of $n$, and hence that $\text{Gal}(F_{n,a}/\mathbb{Q})=S_n$ for a density-one set of $n$. To obtain irreducibility with density one, we use a result of Shorey and Tijdeman, as well as a smooth-number density argument. Following that, two explicitly chosen Newton polygons give cycles that force primitivity, and hence containment of $A_n$. Finally, an exact computation of the valuation of the discriminant at primes satisfying $\frac n2+a<p<n+a$ implies that the discriminant is a nonsquare for odd $a$ and almost all $n$, implying the group is $S_n$ in those cases. For even $a$, we contradict the existence of many square discriminants by showing they generate a family of biased Dirichlet characters. These imply many zeros off of the critical line, which contradict standard zero-density bounds.

papers.title: Borel's computation of the ranks of $K$-theory revisited
papers.abstract: We reprove Borel's computation of the rank of the $K$-groups of rings of algebraic integers $\mathcal{O}_F$ for certain number fields, e.g., $F = \mathbb{Q}(\mu_{l^k})$ for $l$ an odd regular prime number. The idea is to recover a simple formula for $l$-adic {\'e}tale cohomology groups of $\mathcal{O}_F$ in terms of Iwasawa theoretic objects without using Borel's result as an input.

papers.title: Class polynomial obstructions to canonical congruences for the smallest parts function
papers.abstract: We resolve an open conjecture by proving that the only "canonical'' Ramanujan congruence primes for the Andrews' smallest parts function, $\operatorname{spt}(n)$, are $\ell= 5, 7, 13$. Building on work of Ahlgren and Kim, we show that any such congruence forces square-index coefficients of certain weakly holomorphic forms of weight $1/2$ to vanish modulo the congruence prime. A normalized Borcherds product converts this into the vanishing of the derivative of a quotient of two oriented CM polynomials on $X_0(6)$. A quaternionic volume estimate in an Eichler order of level $6$ prevents that vanishing when a suitable inert discriminant is small. Trevi\~no's character estimate supplies such a discriminant for every prime at least $10^{11}$. The remaining range is covered by the previous calculations of Ahlgren and Kim. These results have been verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

papers.title: Quantum Variance for Hecke--Maass Cusp Forms on the Vertical Geodesic
papers.abstract: Let $X=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)\backslash\mathbb H$, and let $\{u_j\}$ be an orthonormal basis of even Hecke--Maass cusp forms on $X$ with Laplace eigenvalues $1/4+t_j^2$. For a real-valued $\psi\in C_c^\infty(0,\infty)$, define \[ \mu_j(\psi)=\int_0^\infty\psi(y)|u_j(iy)|^2\,\frac{dy}{y}, \qquad M(\psi)=\frac6\pi\int_0^\infty\psi(y)\,\frac{dy}{y}. \] For $T\ge2$, $1\le U\le T$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove \[ \sum_{\substack{u_j\ {\rm even}\\T<t_j\le T+U}} L(1,\mathrm{sym}^2u_j)|\mu_j(\psi)-M(\psi)|^2 \ll_{\psi,\varepsilon}T^{1+\varepsilon}. \] As a consequence, for fixed $0<\theta\le1$, $0<\eta<\theta/2$, and every $\varepsilon>0$, if $T^\theta\le U\le T$, then all but \[ O_{\psi,\theta,\eta,\varepsilon} \!\left(T^{1+2\eta+\varepsilon}\right) \] of the even forms with $T<t_j\le T+U$ satisfy $\mu_j(\psi)=M(\psi)+O(T^{-\eta})$. In particular, the exceptional proportion tends to zero in this short spectral interval.

papers.title: Non-vanishing of central values of angular Hecke $L$-functions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we evaluate asymptotically the first and second moment of central values of the family of Hecke $L$-functions associated to angular characters over imaginary quadratic number fields of class number one. We use our results to deduce a non-vanishing result concerning these $L$-functions.

papers.title: On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation
papers.abstract: We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.

papers.title: Small values of the Riemann zeta-function near the critical line
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann Hypothesis, we study negative moments and small values of the Riemann zeta-function to the right of the critical line. For every fixed $0<k<1/2$, we establish the conjecturally sharp bound $$ \frac1T\int_T^{2T} \Big|\zeta(\tfrac12+\alpha+it)\Big|^{-2k}\,dt \ll \alpha^{-k^2}, $$ for $\alpha=o(1)$ and $\alpha\gg 1/\log T$. We also obtain almost sharp upper bounds slightly to the left of $1/\log T$. This improves the upper bounds of the first two authors for shifts as small as $1/\log T$, confirming a conjecture of Gonek in this range. A separate bound for the moment at $k=1/2$ yields an improved bound for cancellation in the M\"obius function. Namely, we show that $$ \sum_{n\leq x}\mu(n) \ll \sqrt{x}\exp \bigg(C\sqrt{\frac{\log x}{\log\log x}}\bigg) $$ for some $C>0$, improving on previous results of Soundararajan, Balazard and de Roton, and of the first two authors. For $t$ chosen uniformly from $[T,2T]$, we also prove that \[ \min_{|h|\leq1} \Big|\zeta\Big(\tfrac12+\alpha+i(t+h)\Big)\Big| =\alpha^{1+o(1)} \] in probability, provided that $\alpha \ll (\log T)^{-c}$ for some fixed $c >0$, and $\alpha\log T/\log\log T\to\infty$. This agrees with the leading order predicted by a minimum analogue of the Fyodorov--Hiary--Keating Conjecture. Further results include bounds for minima on intervals of logarithmically growing length, for negative moments in almost all short intervals, and an extension of the range of sharp negative-moment bounds for $k>1/2$. A main ingredient in the proof of some of these results is a Gaussian large-deviation upper bound for $\log|\zeta(1/2+\alpha+it)|^{-1}$, obtained by building on work of Arguin, Bailey, and Roberts.

papers.title: A determinant formula for multiple harmonic sums and their linear independence
papers.abstract: We explicitly evaluate a family of determinants whose entries are multiple harmonic sums. As a consequence, we prove that certain finite sequences of multiple harmonic sums are linearly independent. This result strengthens the previously known linear independence of the corresponding infinite sequences and stands in contrast to the abundance of linear relations among multiple zeta values.

papers.title: Dense Sets with Prescribed Difference Representation Functions
papers.abstract: For a set $A$ of positive integers, let $d_A(n)$ denote the number of representations of $n$ as a difference of two elements of $A$. We prove that, if $\liminf_{n\to\infty}f(n)\geq2$, then for every Sidon set $B$ and every positive function $\omega(x)$ tending to infinity there is a set $A\subseteq\N$ such that $d_A(n)=f(n)$ for all $n\in\N$ and $|A(x)-B(x/2)|\leq\omega(x)$ for all $x\geq1$. We also give two extensions that allow $f(n)=1$ for infinitely many $n$. For an infinite Sidon set $B$, the same density scale $B(x/2)$ is retained when $f$ is at least $2$ on arbitrarily long intervals centered at elements of $2B$. If $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals, the density scale $B(x/3)$ is obtained for every Sidon set $B$. The proofs use remote insertion of new representations together with controlled deletions from a Sidon core. As a quantitative consequence, Ruzsa's dense infinite Sidon sequence gives $A(x)=x^{\sqrt2-1+o(1)}$ whenever $\{n:f(n)\geq2\}$ contains arbitrarily long intervals.

papers.title: New Directions in Irrationality
papers.abstract: Since Ap\'ery's proof of the irrationality of $\zeta(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Ap\'ery as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $\mu(\zeta(2))<4.62675$ and $\mu(\zeta(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,\zeta(3),\zeta(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $\mu(A\zeta(3)+B\zeta(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,\zeta(2),\zeta(3),\ldots,\zeta(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.

papers.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
papers.abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindel\"of-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

papers.title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.

papers.title: Theta Relations
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical quartic and cubic theta identities, we establish a product formula for Siegel--Jacobi theta series associated with rationally isometric positive-definite quadratic spaces. Our main theorem expresses a product of theta series of arbitrary Siegel degree as a finite double character sum over quotients of commensurable lattices. For the root lattice $A_2$, it yields a finite Fourier identity for cubes of cubic theta functions, a new proof of the two-variable cubic identity, and seven independent relations in degree two. A second specialization gives a new square analogue of the two-variable cubic identity. At the origin it reduces to $a(q)a(q^2)=b(q)b(q^2)+c(q)c(q^2)$; in degree two, the same seven relation patterns recur with each cube replaced by the corresponding product at $\tau$ and $2\tau$. We further extend the cubic identities on $A_2$ to $\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq3$, and to $2\ell$-th-power identities on $A_{\ell-1}$ for every $\ell\geq2$, in arbitrary Siegel degree. The doubled-order construction recovers Jacobi's quartic identity and gives its analogues in arbitrary Siegel degree.

papers.title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.

papers.title: Uncountably many settled elements are never Frobenius elements
papers.abstract: Boston and Jones conjectured that given a number field $K$, a quadratic polynomial $f\in K[x]$, and an element $\alpha\in K$ such that the arboreal Galois representation $\rho_{f,\alpha}:\text{Gal}(\overline{K}/K)\to \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$ attached to the pair $(f,\alpha)$ is well defined, any element in the image of such representation that is a Frobenius for an unramified prime of $K$ is a settled element. We exhibit an explicit uncountable subset $S\subseteq \text{Aut}(T_\infty)$, consisting of pairwise non-conjugate settled elements, such that no matter how $K,f,\alpha$ are chosen, no element of $S$ can be a Frobenius for any ramified or unramified prime of $K$.
